title: Find the Peak
statement:
`heights` describes a mountain trail: the heights **strictly increase up to one peak and then strictly decrease** (so there are at least 3 values, and the peak is never the first or last one).

Return the **index of the peak**.
constraints: heights strictly increases and then strictly decreases

examples.explanation: 2 is the highest and sits at index 1.

hints.nudge: Look at the middle element and the one after it. Are you going uphill or downhill there?
hints.pattern: Binary search on the slope: compare heights[mid] with heights[mid + 1].
hints.pseudocode:
lo = 0; hi = n - 1
while lo < hi:
  mid = (lo + hi) / 2
  if heights[mid] < heights[mid + 1]: lo = mid + 1   // still climbing: peak is to the right
  else: hi = mid                                      // descending: peak is at mid or to the left
return lo
hints.walkthrough: A scan for the maximum is O(n). On this trail, if heights[mid] < heights[mid + 1] you are on the way up, so the peak is to the right of mid. Otherwise you are on the way down (or at the peak), so the peak is at mid or to its left. Keep shrinking the range; when it has one element left, that is the peak. O(log n).
